title: Web page chats are deleted after 90 days only by chance, so visitors' chats and numbers can stay for good
what: The AI helper on a gym's web page promises that a visitor's chat is deleted 90 days after its last message. No nightly job does that deletion. It runs only on about 1 in 50 new visitor questions, from any gym. If visitor chats slow down or stop, old chats with visitors' words, and the enquiry left from a chat with no number, stay with no end, and nobody notices. A chat that fails to clear writes only a warning in the database log, and it is tried again first every time, so a few stuck chats can block the clean-up. Not live yet (the web page AI helper is hidden).
expected: The 90-day clean-up runs every night with the other clean-ups, and a failure is reported.
how_often: whenever a gym's page gets few new chats
fix_line: Call the 90-day chat clean-up from the nightly job and log when it fails

title: A browser alert that fails to send is never tried again
what: Every minute the server marks waiting gym alerts as sent and only then hands them to the sender. If the push service is busy or the line drops, the alert is lost: it stays marked as sent, the run only adds one to a failed count in a passing log line, and it is never retried. A gym with many staff browsers can also have alerts handed over that the run has no room left to send, and those are lost the same way. Staff with the admin app closed miss the alert, even an urgent one such as a complaint; it is still in the bell when they next open the app.
expected: An alert is marked sent only after a browser took it, and a failed send is tried again for a short while.
how_often: whenever the push service or the line fails for a moment
fix_line: Mark alerts sent after the push succeeds and retry failed ones

title: Plan-end reminders are used up before any message goes, and a missed night skips one
what: The nightly billing job marks each 7, 3 and 1 day plan-end reminder as done in the database before anything is sent. Today no message is built, so every reminder is used up with nothing sent. When messages are built, one that fails is never sent again. The job only looks for gyms exactly 7, 3 or 1 days from the end, so if the job fails one night, that day's reminder is skipped for good, with only a hidden log line. Not live yet (online buying is off).
expected: A reminder is marked done only after it was sent, and a missed night is caught up the next night.
how_often: every reminder today; later on any failed send or missed night
fix_line: Mark reminders done after sending and look for any reminder day passed

title: MettleUp cannot see how online joining, free trials and gym web pages work out
what: The server keeps every online join request, every free-trial request, every web page question and every web page chat, but nothing counts them for MettleUp. Nobody can tell how many people join online, how many trials become paying members, or whether gym web pages bring any members. Decisions on these features, and on whether to sell them, are made blind.
expected: HQ shows a few numbers per week across all gyms: online join requests and how many became members, trials and how many paid, and web page questions and chats.
fix_line: Add weekly totals for online joins, trials and web page use to HQ

items.reason: these database files hold no timer, recording, heart-rate or watch code; only server jobs, checked under L6.5
